[[VIDEOID:98deb47ca077beb0ee3f4fde6ce89212]] I was looking for a powerful yet quiet induction cooktop.  I first decided to buy the Secura 9100MC 1800W.  Once I got it, I turned on and it worked great, but fan was really loud and it distracted me while I was cooking.  So I decided to return the Secura 9100MC 1800W and bought the Ivation 1800 Watt model IVICGT18B. I read some reviews on this unit on Amazon and some reviewers said it was fairly quiet compared to other induction cooktops.  So I was excited to receive the Ivation and see for myself.  However, I was disappointed because when I turned on the unit, the fan made really loud noises but the noise seemed like the fan was not seated properly.  I posted a video of the noise for you to see and hear what I had experienced.  If I turned it upside down, the horrible fan noise would go away.  Atlas I was so disappointed, but I wanted to give the Ivation another shot since I think I just happen to receive a defective unit since the fan worked as intended if I turn the unit upside down.  So I returned it and got a replacement.  My replacement came and I was a bit nervous to turn it on, but to my surprise there was no horrible fan noise but rather a soft whisper of a fan, and more quiet than the Secura 9100MC 1800W.  Let's see how long my Ivation's fan last and if it last then I would give it 5 stars.  I am using the Ivation cooktop with the HCX 32 cm Shabu Shabu Dual Sided Hot Pot With Divider. Positives: Character design templates are included and easy to follow; Unpacking of the product is quick and easy, no hard-to-cut plastic covered items; Once you work through the initial faults of this product(see negatives), it is fun and my son was excited to create characters.
Negatives: Design flaw #1: Instructions are to press firmly and beads will stay. Well, they don't. When you use the included paper template, the beads don't stay and topple over. My son was initially very frustrated with this until we came up with our own solution. Our solution was to fold up a paper towel, get it wet, and we dabbed the bottom of each bead before sticking it on to the template. The beads seemed to stay much better once they had a little bit of "glue" to help them stick. Design flaw #2: The container that you separate the beads in to by color has no top. Once we were done for the day, we dumped the remaining beads into a baggy because the nice little separating container they give you doesn't have a top. Weird. Why wouldn't they supply a top???
Last comment: Neither a positive nor a negative...just an opinion. The spinning drying thing is not totally necessary. Sure, my son had fun pushing the button twenty times to make it spin; That was fun. The directions said it gets rid of the excess water, but you have to wait at least 20 min (according to the directions) for them to dry anyway. We waited longer because ours were still sticky.
